subject.title: Surface internal system messages in a distinct UI block instead of normal chat bubbles

question: Should OpenClaw hide internal/runtime-originated messages by default, or expose selected runtime notices in a dedicated diagnostic/system UI block?
rationale: Current source can still render system-shaped rows through normal chat grouping, but deciding which runtime messages are visible is a product/API boundary choice rather than a mechanical UI-only fix.

options.title: Audience contract first
options.body: Define agent-only versus visible-diagnostic provenance, hide agent-only internals, then render only intentional runtime notices in a distinct system block.

options.title: Hide all internals from chat
options.body: Treat system/runtime messages as logs or diagnostics only and keep the main transcript strictly user/assistant visible.

options.title: Style current system rows only
options.body: Add a visual system treatment for existing system-role rows without changing upstream audience/provenance semantics.

recommendation.title: Audience contract first
recommendation.body: Define agent-only versus visible-diagnostic provenance, hide agent-only internals, then render only intentional runtime notices in a distinct system block.

likelyOwner.reason: The current UI and Gateway display-projection history points to steipete as the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-surface product decision.
